URL: (compiled) Wednesday 14 October 2026 EVENING ticker basis
Primary: CNBC quote endpoint, read 18:06 BST.

*** PROVENANCE NOTE — THIS EDITION WAS NOT BUILT THE USUAL WAY ***
The scheduled LaunchAgent run started on time at 17:55 and was healthy, not hung. It had already written
a complete evening edition into index.html — 5 GEO + 5 UK, a Wednesday PMQs section, 52 cache files and a
sources appendix — and the validator passed it on all checks including 12 distinct outlets. It was stopped
at 18:03 only because a second, manual edition for the same date would have collided with it.
The edition was reviewed rather than rebuilt. Spot-checks traced every load-bearing figure back to its own
cache: American inflation at 3.7% from 3.4% in August, 600,000 left without electricity in Ukraine, the
900,000 workers in the bogus self-employment consultation (gov.uk), the IEA's 2027 diesel horizon, and the
container ship sinking in Hormuz. None was invented. The vetoed features were correctly absent — no
war-day-count block and no change-diff line, despite the scheduled prompt still instructing it to add the
former.

*** WHAT I CHANGED: MARKETS AND THE TIMESTAMP ***
The run's figures were accurate when it wrote them at about 17:55 but had drifted by the time of
publication ten minutes later. Gold had fallen a further $23 and bitcoin moved about 200. Rather than
publish a ten-minute-old ticker, all ten instruments were re-read live at 18:06 and the edition and the
embedded-markets block were rewritten together.
  As written 17:55 -> as published 18:10
  Gold   4,104.80 -1.74  ->  4,080.92 -1.82
  BTC      81,762 -1.66  ->    81,997 -1.38
  Brent    106.53 +0.79  ->    106.58 +0.84
  SP     7,722.63 -1.06  ->  7,721.93 -1.07
  VIX       16.52 +8.19  ->     16.54 +8.32
  FTSE  10,724.86 +0.70  -> unchanged, this is the 16:35 close
The timestamp was moved from 17:55 to 18:10, the actual publication time. THE REPLACEMENT WAS SCOPED to
the 14 October evening block: the 10 October evening edition also carries data-time="17:55", and a blanket
replace would have corrupted it. That was checked before and after.

*** THE DAY IN THE TICKER: A RISK-OFF SESSION THAT THE FTSE SAT OUT ***
VIX up 8.3% to 16.54, its sharpest rise in weeks and the first time it has been above 16 this month.
S&P 500 down 1.07%. Gold down 1.82%. Sterling down 0.75% to 1.3153, giving back three sessions of gains.
Bitcoin down 1.38%. American inflation came in at 3.7%, above expectations, three weeks before the
midterms — the obvious candidate for all of the above, and the edition carries it.
Against that, the FTSE CLOSED UP 0.70% at 10,724.86, its best level of the month. A London market rising
on a day when New York fell more than a per cent is worth noting rather than smoothing over; the index is
energy- and defence-heavy and Brent closed higher for a second session.
The gilt barely moved, down about one basis point to 5.42%, holding near its highest since 2007 with the
Budget fourteen days away. The Treasury went the other way, up a basis point to 5.23%.
